title: Optogenetic-mediated induction and monitoring of α-synuclein aggregation in cellular models of Parkinson’s disease
protocol: Mix calcium chloride solution with DNA plasmid solution.
Incubate the mixture for 20 minutes at room temperature to form precipitate.
Add the precipitate drop-wise to HEK293T cells in a 35-mm dish containing serum-free medium.
Incubate the cells overnight at 37°C in a CO2 incubator with 5% CO2.
Replace the transfection mixture with fresh growth media the next day.
Culture the transfected cells for an additional day to ensure high expression levels of LIPA constructs.
Plate 0.6 × 10^5 cells/cm² of HEK293T cells in a 35-mm plate in 1 mL of DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin (P/S).
Incubate the cells for 16 hours at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Replace media with fresh DMEM containing 10% FBS and 1% P/S two hours prior to transfection.
Add plasmid DNA to the tube: LIPA-α-syn (1 μg), LIPA-α-synΔNAC (1.6 μg), or LIPA-empty (0.8 μg).
Add 25 μL of sterile ddH₂O.
Add 25 μL of 0.5 M CaCl₂ and mix well by pipetting.
While vortexing, add 50 μL of 2× HeBS dropwise.
Use a high-speed shaking vortex to ensure efficient DNA-calcium phosphate co-precipitation.
Incubate the precipitate at 20°C–22°C for at least 10 min, not exceeding 15 min.
Add the mix dropwise to the cells (100 μL/dish).
Gently swirl the plate until the medium color is uniform red again.
Do not exceed a total volume of added mix that exceeds 10% of the culture media volume in the well.
Incubate the plate with the transfection mix for a minimum of 5 h or a maximum of 16 h.
Aspirate the medium after an incubation time of 5 h and slowly add fresh medium to the plate.
Illuminate cells under blue light (469 nm) at 0.8 mW/mm² for periods of (0, 6, 12, and 24 hours).
Use blue light at an intensity between 0.3 mW/mm² and 0.8 mW/mm².
Set stimulation duration from 1 minute to 48 hours.
Measure light intensity at the bottom of the culture plate using a power meter.
Ensure that blue light intensity of 0.8 mW/mm² for up to 48 hours is below phototoxicity threshold.
Optimize light intensity and duration for induction of inclusions, using an intensity of 0.3 mW/mm² for up to 48 hours to avoid significant toxicity.
Induce LIPA-α-syn aggregates in mammalian cells or iPSC-derived neurons.
Proceed with biochemical characterization of the induced α-syn inclusions.
Detect high molecular weight (HMW) α-syn aggregated species spanning approximately from 180 to 370 kDa on a Western blot.
Remove the media from cells exposed to blue light.
Wash cells twice with ice-cold dPBS (Ca+/Mg+).
Add 250 μl of 2× Laemmli buffer directly to the plate for cell lysis.
Scrape the cells.
Collect the cell lysate.
Transfer the cell lysate into a microcentrifuge tube.
Use RIPA buffer for protein extraction from cells as an alternative method.
Store RIPA buffer at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Add protease and phosphatase inhibitors, PMSF, and 1 mM DTT prior to cell lysis.
Proceed with cell lysis on ice using gentle trituration.
Heat samples in RIPA buffer at 70°C for 10 minutes before loading into Western blot gel.
Store protein samples at -20°C for up to 7 days after snap freezing on dry ice.
For longer storage, store samples at -80°C.
Use 4%-20% precast polyacrylamide gradient gels for proper visualization of LIPA-α-syn HMW species.
Use home-made 10% acrylamide SDS-PAGE gels as an alternative method to visualize LIPA-α-syn aggregates.
Heat samples for 15 min at 95°C to denature proteins and DNA.
Load 5-10 μL of each sample per well, corresponding to 10-20 μg of protein.
Allow the samples to migrate for 45 min at 160 V in 1× Running Buffer.
Use a Chameleon Duo ladder as a molecular weight marker to estimate the molecular weight of proteins and monitor electrophoresis progress.
Follow a wet-transfer protein transfer protocol to transfer the protein from the gel to a 0.2 μm pore nitrocellulose membrane.
Mount and soak all components in cold 1× transfer buffer.
Assemble the transfer “sandwich” in a transfer cassette.
Pack pre-wet nitrocellulose membrane and gel together inside one pre-wet sponge followed by one Whatman filter paper.
Place the gel facing the negative electrode, with the nitrocellulose membrane facing the cathode.
Remove air bubbles from the assembled transfer stack components.
Place the transfer cassette inside the transfer tank.
Add a magnet to the bottom of the apparatus for constant stirring at low speed.
Put an ice block in the transfer tank to maintain cold buffer temperature.
Place the transfer tank in a bucket and add ice to ensure even temperature distribution during the protocol.
Perform the transfer protocol at 4°C.
Wet PVDF membranes in methanol.
Run the transfer for 2 h at 350 mA.
Rinse the membrane in 1× PBS.
Heat the membrane in a microwave with approximately 50 mL of PBS at 500 W for 1 min.
Allow the membrane to cool down to 20°C–22°C before proceeding.
Block the membranes for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in WB blocking buffer under constant rocking.
Incubate membranes for a minimum of 2 hours at 20°C–22°C with anti-α-syn antibody diluted at 1:1000 in WB blocking buffer.
Wash the membrane with WB washing buffer three times for 5 minutes each under constant rocking.
Incubate the membrane for a minimum of 1 hour with an anti-mouse 680RD LI-COR secondary antibody diluted at 1:10000 in WB blocking buffer.
Wash the membrane with WB washing buffer three times for 5 minutes each under constant rocking.
Detect protein bands using an Odyssey CLx Infrared Imaging System using the IR680 channel.
Image both channels (IR680 and 800) to visualize all the bands of the molecular weight marker.
Incubate membranes with anti-mCherry antibody diluted at 1:2000 in WB blocking buffer for a minimum of 2 hours at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the membrane with WB washing buffer three times for 5 minutes each under constant rocking.
Incubate the membrane with an anti-rabbit 800CW LI-COR secondary antibody diluted at 1:10000 in WB blocking buffer for a minimum of 1 hour.
Wash the membrane with WB washing buffer three times for 5 minutes each under constant rocking.
Evaluate and quantify the smear corresponding to the LIPA-α-syn aggregates using Image Studio Software or Empiria Studio Software from LI-COR.
Dilute an antibody raised against the pathological form of α-syn phosphorylated at residue serine 129 (pS129) at 1:2000.
Incubate with anti-β-actin antibody diluted at 1:5000 on the same membrane for loading control.
Use an anti-mouse 800CW LI-COR antibody diluted at 1:10000 in WB blocking buffer.
Remove the media of cells exposed to the blue light.
Wash cells twice with 2 mL of cold dPBS (Ca+/Mg+).
Add 250 μL of Lysis buffer to a 35-mm plate.
Scrape cells off the dish using a cell scrapper and transfer into a microcentrifuge tube.
Pause point: Samples can be stored at −80°C for 2–4 days after a snap freeze on dry ice.
Lyse the cells using a Dremel tissue homogenizer.
Centrifuge samples at 500 × g for 5 min to pellet the nuclear fraction.
Collect the supernatant and centrifuge at 1000 × g for 10 min to clarify the fraction.
Collect the supernatant and place it on ice.
Mount the vacuum manifold using two thin Whatman filter papers pre-soaked with 1× PBS, 1.5% SDS.
Assemble the vacuum manifold with a 0.2 μm pore size acetate membrane pre-soaked in 1× PBS containing 1.5% SDS on top of the filter paper.
Tightly close the vacuum manifold and apply vacuum to check for proper tightening.
Turn off the vacuum.
Put aside 20% of the volume of cell lysate collected from each experimental condition.
Use half of this volume as a loading control and run it in Western blot on a nitrocellulose membrane to evaluate the total amount of LIPA protein.
Deplete the other half of the volume from LIPA-α-syn aggregates by adding SDS to reach 1.5% final concentration.
Heat the sample for 15 min at 95°C to denature the protein.
Add SDS to samples from step 34 to reach 1.5% SDS final concentration and incubate for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Load 100 μL of 1.5% SDS solution in each well and apply vacuum until buffer passes through the filter.
Wait until filtration is complete.
Ensure that the wells are not entirely dried before loading the sample.
Quickly load 50 μL of samples from step 34 into each well.
Fill empty wells with a 1.5% SDS solution.
Apply vacuum to filter the samples until complete passage.
Load 100 μL of 1.5% SDS solution into the wells and apply vacuum again.
Wait until complete passage before turning off the vacuum.
Repeat this washing step at least once as necessary.
Unmount the vacuum manifold, take the acetate membrane and rinse it in Milli-Q water.
Place the membrane in PBS at 4°C while running the loading controls.
Use a 0.2 μm pore Nitrocellulose membrane.
Place the membrane into a flat-bottom container with protein side up.
Stain the membrane in Ponceau red solution and place on a rocker.
Rinse the membrane quickly with distilled H2O (dH2O).
Wash the membrane repeatedly in 1× PBS until achieving a clear total protein stain.
Image the membrane to assess total protein levels in each condition.
Visualize and quantify the filter retardation signal using the LI-COR Odyssey Imager and Image Studio Software.
Remove the media from cells exposed to blue light.
Wash the cells twice with 2 mL of cold dPBS Ca+ Mg+.
Follow lysis and centrifugation steps as described for filter retardation.
Keep 10% of the sample volume for detection of total protein levels by Western blot.
Determine the volume of the supernatant.
Mix the supernatant with SDD-AGE sample buffer.
Incubate the sample mix at 20°C–22°C for 7 minutes.
Load samples onto a 1.8% agarose gel prepared in buffer G containing 0.02% SDS.
Run the SDD-AGE in buffer G containing 0.01% SDS at 12V/cm at 20°C–22°C for 2 hours until the dye front reaches the end of the gel.
Transfer the gel into a nitrocellulose membrane using the Turbo transfer method from Bio-Rad.
Follow the steps described in the Western blot protocol for visualization and quantification of aggregates.
Perform in vitro seeding experiments using RT-QuIC.
Remove the media from cells exposed to blue light.
Wash cells twice with 2 mL cold dPBS Ca+ Mg+.
Follow lysis and centrifugation steps as described in steps 29–34.
Subject clarified lysate to ultracentrifugation at 150,000 × g for 1 h at 4°C.
Resuspend pellet from ultracentrifugation step in 150 μL PBS.
Sonicate the resuspended pellet at 30% intensity, 1 s on and 1 s off, for 45 s using a Fisherbrand Model 505 sonicator.
Repeat sonication if the pellet remains visible up to two times.
Confirm absence of the pellet by pipetting.
Determine protein concentration of the cell pellet using Pierce BCA Protein Assay Kits.
Dilute samples to reach a final concentration of 2 μg/mL.
Add 200 μL RT-QuIC reaction mixture containing monomeric α-syn to each well in black clear bottom 96-well plate.
Carefully pipette 2 μg/mL LIPA-α-syn aggregates into the mixture.
Mix 2 μg/mL of LIPA-α-syn monomers purified from cells not exposed to blue light for negative control condition.
Pipette recombinant monomeric α-syn alone into wells containing RT-QuIC reaction mixture for experimental control.
Cover plates with sealing film and manually remove any creases.
Place the covered plates in a plate reader.
Set up the plate reader program as described in Table 1.
Preheat the plate to reach an optimal temperature of 41°C before starting the experiment.
Use alternative plate readers, such as the FLUOstar OMEGA plate reader (BMG Labtech, Germany), for RT-QuIC experiments if necessary.
Allow the program used in step 64 to run for up to 1 week.
Measure Th-T fluorescence (excitation 435 nm; emission 485 nm) every 30 min using BioTek Cytation 5 Multi-Mode Readers plate reader.
Record and graph fluorescence against time, depicting a typical exponential curve characterized by a lag phase and plateau.
Set the positive RT-QuIC seeding reaction threshold at three times the initial fluorescence intensity recorded at time 0 h.
Plate 0.8 × 10^5 cells/cm² of HEK293T cells on poly-L-lysine-coated 12-mm coverslips in a 24-well plate with DMEM, 10% FBS, and 1% P/S.
Incubate the plated cells for 16 hours at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Transfect the cells using previously described methods, with DNA ratios adjusted to obtain equal protein expression levels across different conditions.
Illuminate the transfected cells for 16 hours under blue light at an intensity of 0.8 mW/mm² to induce LIPA aggregation.
Fix the illuminated cells by incubating them in a solution containing 4% (w/v) paraformaldehyde and 3% (w/v) sucrose for 15 minutes at 20°C–22°C.
Wash the cells three times with 1× PBS for 5 min each.
Permeabilize the cells using a solution of 0.3% (v/v) Triton X-100 in 1× PBS for 10 min at 20°C–22°C.
Rinse the cells once with 1× PBS to remove any remaining Triton.
Incubate cells for 1 h at 20°C–22°C in ICC blocking buffer.
Incubate cells with primary antibodies raised against pS129, ubiquitin, p62 or hsp70 diluted in blocking solution at 4°C for 16 h.
Perform three 10-min washes with fresh blocking buffer.
Incubate cells in secondary antibodies (Alexa Fluor 488 or 633) diluted at 1:400 for 1 h at 20°C–22°C.
Perform two 10-min washes with 1× PBS.
Stain the cell nuclei with DAPI at 1:5000 to reach 1 μg/mL in 1× PBS for 2 min.
Perform two quick washes with 1× PBS.
Quickly rinse the coverslips with dH2O to remove any residual salt.
Mount the 12-mm coverslips onto a microscope slide using 4.5 μL of mounting media.
Image LB-markers staining using confocal microscope.
Plate 0.8 × 10^5 cells/cm^2 of HEK293T cells on a pre-coated glass-bottom imaging chamber such as a 35-mm MatTek dish.
Replace the cell culture media with pre-warmed (37°C) live-cell imaging medium one hour prior to the start of the experiment.
Mount the stage-top incubator on top of the Super Z Galvo stage.
Fill the stage-top incubator with 15 mL of sterile ddH2O.
Open the CO2 cylinder and adjust the percentage to 5% CO2.
Wait for 10 min for CO2 stabilization.
Turn-on the stage heating and top heating.
Set the stage at 40°C and the top at 43°C.
Attach the lens heater to the objective and turn-on the controller if using a lens heater.
Place a drop of immersion oil (type F) on the lens.
Immediately place the live-cell chamber inside the holders of the stage-top incubator.
Close the stage-top incubator and use the cursor to get the object into focus.
Wait for 15–30 min before redoing the focus.
Set one sequence of image acquisition meant to stimulate and record the mCherry signal corresponding to the LIPA.
Set the WLL at 587 nm.
Open a HyD detector to capture signals ranging from 595 to 650 nm.
Add a WLL laser at 470 nm to stimulate LIPA aggregation.
Choose a cell expressing high levels of mCherry.
Start an image trial with the laser power set at 30% or less.
Acquire a Z-stack overtime using a scan speed between 400 and 8000 Hz.
Optimize imaging parameters to minimize phototoxicity while maintaining good resolution.
Thaw a lentiviral tube from -80°C and place it on ice.
Prepare a master mix of cell culture medium (STEMdiff Maturation media) coupled with lentiviral particles to reach a multiplicity of infection of 10 (MOI = 10).
Slowly add the maturation media containing the viral particles to the neurons.
Incubate for 7-10 days, changing half the media every 4 days.
Check cells every day for mCherry signal expression starting seven days post infection.
Observe the peak viral expression, typically 2 days after the initial detection of mCherry signal.
Start analysis at the peak of expression.
Do not wait longer than 4 days to avoid cellular stress and the appearance of stress granules.
Establish stable cell lines expressing LIPA backbones using pCMV lentivirus for high-level expression in mammalian cells.
Select cells with stable transgene expression by applying puromycin selection pressure.
Establish the ideal dosage of puromycin for the specific target cell line.
Plate cells at 20% confluency in a 6-well plate.
Incubate the plated cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Thaw a tube of lentiviral particles on ice from −80°C.
Dilute polybrene to reach a final concentration of 10 μg/mL in cell culture media.
Add lentiviral particles diluted to reach a MOI of 1, 10 or 100 to the medium with polybrene.
Incubate cells with the medium containing viral particles at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 3 days.
Split each confluent well into six wells in complete cell culture medium after 3 days.
Incubate the split cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 16 hours.
Expose cells to increasing concentrations of puromycin (1–1.5–2–2.5–3–5 μg/mL).
Sort cells using a flow cytometer for mCherry expressing cells, keeping the 30% highly expressing cells.
Plate sorted cells in two T25 flasks; one for cryopreservation and the other for monoclonal selection.
When the T25 flask is 70% confluent, passage the cells to plate 100 cells in a 10-cm dish.
Incubate for 3–5 days at 37°C and 5% CO2 to allow colonies to grow.
Under a fluorescent microscope, look for colonies with the highest expression of mCherry that are well spaced.
Circle the colony with a pen when a desired colony is found.
Scrape the colony with a pipette tip set to 15 μL.
Aspirate the scraped colony from the dish.
Transfer the selected colony to an empty well of a 96-well plate.
Add 150 μL of medium to each well of a 96-well plate.
Repeat until at least 20 colonies have been selected from the 10-cm plate.
Incubate the 96-well plate for 5–7 days at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Change media every 3 days during incubation.
Expand the culture when cells reach confluency in a T75 flask.
Cryopreserve the cells as soon as they reach 70% confluency.
Keep monoclonal LIPA clones protected from ambient white light.
Passage the cells every 3–4 days to avoid overconfluence.
Plate cells stably expressing LIPA backbones 12–16 hours before blue light exposure.
Illuminate cells 12 hours post plating for optimal aggregation.
